bc_split_beaver.blurb: A small cliff within the Smoke Bluffs in Squamish, sitting up the slope from the left end of the Penny Lane wall. Only six climbs here, five of them trad crack lines from 5.7 up to 5.10 and a single sport line in the low 5.11 range. What sets it apart in this park is the angle: several of the cracks are vertical or lean past vertical, where most of the surrounding bluffs are lower-angle. It suits a trad climber who has a rack and wants a few short, steep jamming pitches between visits to the busier sections.
bc_split_beaver.approach: From the staircase near Pixie Corner, follow a side path to the right at the top. After a few hundred feet a smaller path forks left up to the cliff. Reaching Ronin's Corner means you overshot.

bc_the_wave_2.blurb: A single sizeable boulder in the Warm Up sector of Hunter Creek bouldering, in the Fraser Valley near Chilliwack. It holds six problems, and the range is wide: an easy V0 or V0-1 warm-up, a pair of V4s, then two hard lines at V7 and V8. Problems tend to start with a stout, burly sequence and relax toward the top. The harder ones lean on underclings, slopers and pinches, with a bulge to get over. Landings are described as good and the boulder is not very tall. Find it by walking past the Warm-Up Boulder on the little trail that loops around to the right.
